patterns_found.visual_evidence: The mobile sketch shows a small boxed icon with horizontal lines in the top-right of the header, a conventional hamburger/menu trigger. The desktop sketch does not show this control.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: Tapping the icon should open and close a navigation panel or menu containing site links. The trigger should expose expanded/collapsed state and likely overlay or push content on small screens.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The sketch does not show whether the opened menu is a dropdown, full-screen overlay, slide-out drawer, or inline expansion, nor what links it contains.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: Because the mobile sketch explicitly includes a hamburger menu trigger, implementing that disclosure/menu interaction implies programmatic focus handling when the menu opens and closes.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: Focus should move predictably to the opened menu or first actionable item, remain usable by keyboard/switch users, and return to the menu button when closed. Escape/close behavior may also be needed depending on menu presentation.
patterns_found.ambiguities: If the mobile menu is only a simple inline expansion, focus handling can be lighter; if it is an overlay/drawer, stronger focus control is required.

sketch_notes: These sketches imply a largely static article/detail page with minimal JavaScript. The only clear interactive requirement is a mobile-only navigation toggle in the header; the desktop version appears to present content without visible interactive widgets, forms, tabs, accordions, or loading mechanisms. Cross-viewport complexity is therefore low, with JS concentrated on responsive navigation behavior and its associated accessibility/focus handling on mobile.
